lesson.content:
## What it is
Satellite communication involves using satellites to transmit signals across the Earth. There are three main types of satellites: Geostationary Orbit (GEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), and Low Earth Orbit (LEO). [p. 2]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine a TV channel that can be received anywhere in the world, even in remote areas, by bouncing signals off satellites. [p. 2]

## How it works
1. **Satellite Positioning**: Satellites are positioned in different orbits to cover the Earth. Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellites stay above one point on the Earth's surface, covering the entire globe. Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) satellites are positioned at a medium altitude, typically used for GPS. Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites are positioned at a lower altitude, used for satellite phones and internet services. [p. 2]
2. **Signal Transmission**: A ground station sends a signal to a satellite. The satellite amplifies the signal and sends it back to another ground station. This process allows for communication across vast distances. [p. 2]

## Key terms
- **GEO (Geostationary)**: Satellites that stay above one point on the Earth's surface, covering the entire globe. [p. 2]
- **MEO (Medium Earth Orbit)**: Satellites positioned at a medium altitude, typically used for GPS. [p. 2]
- **LEO (Low Earth Orbit)**: Satellites positioned at a lower altitude, used for satellite phones and internet services. [p. 2]

## Example
A satellite in GEO orbit can cover a large area, such as the entire United States, with minimal signal loss. [p. 2]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 2]

## Exam tip
Examiners often ask about the different types of satellites and their applications. Make sure to distinguish between GEO, MEO, and LEO satellites and their respective uses. [p. 2]
